title: Runtime Traps and Force Unwrapping DoS
platform_conditions: Swift runtime language semantics (optional unwrapping, overflow trapping, preconditions); applies wherever Swift runs (iOS/macOS and server-side Swift)
security_mechanism: Several Swift constructs are defined to abort the process rather than return an error: '!' on nil and 'as!' on a wrong dynamic type trap; subscripting an array out of bounds traps; '+'/'*' on integers overflow-trap in every build configuration; 'try!' rethrows the error as a fatal; precondition/fatalError are unconditional aborts. One attacker-chosen value reaching any of them — a missing JSON field, a number above Int64, an index past the end — kills the whole process (on iOS the app crashes for the user; on a Swift server the worker dies), so a single malformed request becomes a reliable remote denial of service with no memory corruption needed. unowned references trap the same way when the target was deallocated by an earlier request's cleanup.

source_sink_clues.source: Fields of decoded JSON/protobuf messages, query parameters, headers, and any numeric or array value the attacker can set (including 0, negative, or >Int64.max values that trigger arithmetic traps).
source_sink_clues.sink: '!' force unwrap and 'as!' forced downcast on decoded values; 'try!' on parsing calls; array/collection subscripts on untrusted indices; arithmetic on attacker-supplied integers without &+ / &* / checked variants; precondition/fatalError reachable from input; unowned access after await

tracking_guards: Check every input-derived optional uses guard let/if let with a handled failure path, conditional 'as?', and get(index) or bounds checks instead of forced forms; check numeric inputs use Int64-clamped parsing or overflow-checked operators; check precondition/fatalError appear only on truly impossible internal invariants not influenced by request data.
not_candidate_when: The forced unwrap sits on a value the app itself just constructed (non-nil by construction, e.g. a just-registered dependency), the decode path already rejects malformed payloads before the subscript, or the crash aborts only an attacker's own single-user session with no shared state (still a hardening note, not a candidate).
synthetic_safe_example: guard let token = json["token"] as? String else { return }
public_references: CWE-755: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html
